# Texture fix visual evidence

These images were generated by running the same GLX diagnostic against:

- Coin `31a4ea1bbd1` (before)
- PR #862, commit `722ec889935` (texture-size limits)
- PR #863, commit `747d63aeef4` (degenerate 3D mipmaps)

The run used Coin's `SoGLImage` and texture-size validation paths with Mesa
llvmpipe 25.2.8. The mipmap pixels were read back from OpenGL after Coin
created the complete texture chain.

The presentation labels were added after capture; the acceptance results and
texture data shown inside the panels come from the corresponding Coin builds.

`texture-size-limits-before-after-v2.svg` is the labeled source for the PNG
embedded in PR #862. Its four outcomes reproduce the Coin results captured by
the diagnostic: `16x16` is accepted in both builds, while `17x16` changes from
accepted to rejected when the configured limit is enforced.

`glimage-upload-target-before-after.png` compares Coin `31a4ea1bbd1` with the
upload-target PrePR at `f3127490888`. The same GLX program traverses a
`SoTexture2` immediately after a `SoTexture3`, then creates a `SoTexture3` on
texture unit 1 while unit 0 does not select 3D. OpenGL readback reports missing
`0x0x0` storage for both cases on the baseline and valid `4x4x1` and `4x4x4`
storage on the candidate. The colored cells and slices are the actual uploaded
texels returned by OpenGL.

`scenetexture2-background-before-after.png` compares Coin `31a4ea1bbd1` with
PR #868 at `40e0af8ef1d`. The same FBO-backed `SoSceneTexture2` first publishes
RGBA `(31,101,233,71)`, then changes only `backgroundColor` to
`(197,41,83,211)`. OpenGL readback still returns the old color on the baseline
and the new color on the candidate. The panels composite the actual returned
RGBA texels over a checkerboard to make their alpha values visible.
